R010 module_java is an Australian-outback predator/prey simulation (Swing GUI). Source = 17 root `.java` files in default package (the `simulation/` and `configuration/` dirs hold only stray `.class` artifacts, not tracked source). Hierarchy: `Animal`(abstract) ← Ant, Dingo, Eagle, Emu, Rat, Snake; `Plant`(abstract) ← Acacia, Grass. `Simulator` keeps separate `List<Animal>`/`List<Plant>`.

**Build:** plain `javac -d <out> *.java` compiles clean (JDK 21). **NON-deterministic**: `Randomizer.getRandom()` returns `new Random()` every call (`useShared=false`), so no golden-hash/fingerprint test is possible — verify by compile + behavior-preserving reasoning only (like [[project_r007_module_java]]).

Pre-existing `-Xlint:all` warnings to ignore: `this-escape` in every constructor that calls a method (setLocation/initialise), plus `rawtypes`/`serial` in FieldStats & SimulatorView. Watch only for NEW warning categories.

Refactors done:
- #1 Template Method on `Animal.act()` — act() skeleton was copy-pasted across all 6 subclasses; lifted to concrete `Animal.act()` with hooks getMaxAge/getBreedingAge/getBreedingProbability/getMaxLitterSize/isActive(time)/findFood/createYoung. Dropped redundant per-birth `young.setGender()` (constructor already sets it).
- #2 Pull Up Constructor Body — identical `super; setGender; randomAge?…` block → `Animal.initialise(boolean)` + hook getInitialFoodLevel(). Removed now-dead `rand` field + Random import from Rat/Ant/Snake/Emu (Dingo/Eagle keep rand — used in fog findFood).
- #3 Cleanup `setGender`/`giveDisease` — were allocating a local `Random` shadowing the shared static `rand` field; switched to the field; collapsed setGender if/else to `isMale = rand.nextInt(2)==1`.
- #4 Extract Superclass `Organism` — lifted alive/field/location + isAlive/setDead/getLocation/setLocation/getField from BOTH Animal and Plant into new `Organism`(abstract); Animal & Plant now `extends Organism`, constructors call `super(field,location)`. Fixed `Animal.spreadDisease` which accessed instance `field` directly → `getField()`. Field.place takes Object so passing `this` works; all moved methods stay `protected` + same-package so cross-class calls (Simulator/Rat eating, etc.) still resolve.

- #5 Consolidate `rand` into Organism — lifted the per-class `private static final Random rand = Randomizer.getRandom()` from Animal/Plant/Dingo/Eagle into a single `protected static final Organism.rand`; removed those 4 fields + their `import java.util.Random`. (Field & Randomizer keep their own rand — not Organisms; Simulator uses locals.) All 6 species + Plant now share one generator; fine under non-determinism.

- #6 De-dup Dingo/Eagle `findFood` fog branches — each had the adjacent-search loop written twice (fog branch + else). Dingo: collapsed to a single guard `if (getFog() && rand.nextInt(2) != 0) return null;` + one loop (RNG-exact: draw happens iff foggy, ==0→search, !=0→skip). Eagle: its fog condition was a NO-OP latent bug — `if (getFog() && rand.nextInt(2)==0){search} else {search}` ran the IDENTICAL search in both branches, so eagle always hunts and fog never mattered; removed the dead conditional → single unconditional loop (drops the unused foggy RNG draw, unobservable under non-determinism). Flagged to user; offered to wire up real fog handicap for Eagle (matching Dingo) as a separate behavior-changing fix if wanted.

Remaining ideas (not yet done): the `spreadDisease`/`giveBirth` adjacent-iteration loops in Animal (Form Template Method); weather (fog/rain) flags could move to Organism; optionally make Eagle's fog actually apply a handicap (behavior change, not yet done).
